commit.message:
test(harness-acp): wait for the notification stream before changing catalog (#25385)

## Background

fixes flaky test

the test connected a client, then immediately changed the tool catalog
and waited for the “tool list changed” notification. The client opens
the stream that carries notifications in the background, a moment after
connecting. On a slow CI machine, the catalog change could happen before
that stream was open, the server dropped the notification, and the test
waited until it timed out

## Summary

the test waits until the notification stream is confirmed open, then
changes the catalog. The notification always has somewhere to go, so the
test passes regardless of machine speed

## End-to-End Verification

call.

feat(baseten): add experimental decision models with image input (#25328)

## Background

Baseten serves its decision models (bison-1, groundhog-1, mammoth-1,
elephant-1, and joey-1) through the Model APIs [System One
endpoint](https://docs.baseten.co/reference/inference-api/system-one),
`POST https://inference.baseten.co/v1/systemone`. The question and
answer shapes match the existing experimental decision providers, but
`@ai-sdk/baseten` has no decision model.

Two properties of the endpoint shape the implementation:

- It accepts only JSON request bodies (`Content-Type:
application/json`).
- It reads images only from a conversation in the state, `{ "messages":
[{ "role": "user", "content": [text and image_url parts] }] }`. Any
other JSON state is rendered as text, so an image placed elsewhere in
JSON returns an answer that does not reflect the image.

bison-1 and groundhog-1, released on November 20, 2026, accept text and
images with a 131,072-token context.

## Summary

- `baseten.decisionModel(modelId)` returns an
`Experimental_DecisionModelV4` (`DecisionBasetenModel`) that posts JSON
to `${baseURL}/systemone`. The five decision models are in the model
catalog with a generated capability table; other IDs are passed through.
Decision models always use the Model APIs base URL and ignore
`modelURL`.
- **State**: a single text or JSON part is sent as is; other text and
JSON combinations are joined with newlines. When the state contains an
image, it is sent as one user message whose content holds the text, JSON
(as text), and image parts in request order. Inline JPEG, PNG, and WebP
images become base64 data URLs (the media type is detected when not
fully specified). `experimental_decide` downloads URL file state before
calling the provider (it requires `experimental_download`), so those
images are sent inline too; URL file data passed to the model directly
is forwarded as is, and the API accepts only HTTPS URLs on Amazon S3,
Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Blob Storage. Audio, video, file
references, and other image types throw `UnsupportedFunctionalityError`
before the request.
- **Questions**: SDK `boolean` questions map to `noul`. When only one of
`true`/`false` criteria is given, the other is sent as `null` (Baseten's
default for that outcome), because the API rejects partial criteria with
`422 Noul criteria must be empty or contain exactly false and true`.
Choice and Score map to their native types; null Choice descriptions and
null Score levels are forwarded, which the API accepts. Box questions
are not supported by the API (`422 Question type must be choice, noul or
score`) and throw before the request.
- **Limits** checked before the request, from Baseten's API reference:
1–255 Choice options, 1–10 Score levels, at most 512 options across
questions (each Choice option and Score level counts as one, each yes/no
question as two), and at most 16 images.
- **Output**: answers at full precision (no `rounding` is declared),
`usage.inputTokens` / `usage.outputTokens` from the API's `usage` (input
tokens include image tokens), and Choice/Score `confidence` and Score
`legend` in `providerMetadata.baseten`. Every question must receive
exactly one answer, or the call throws `InvalidResponseDataError`.
- `maxOutputTokens`, `reasoning`, and `providerOptions.baseten` produce
unsupported warnings and are not sent.
- The shared error schema moves from `baseten-provider.ts` to
`baseten-error.ts` (unchanged) so the decision model can use it without
a circular import; it gains a `postJsonToApi` failed-response handler.
- Docs (Decision Models section and capability table), examples
(`decide/baseten/basic.ts`, `decide/baseten/image.ts`), and a patch
changeset.

## Manual Verification

Against the live Model APIs:

- **Text**: all five models with single-text, single-JSON-object, and
text-plus-JSON state, each with Choice, Boolean (with and without
criteria), and Score questions. Every request returned one answer per
question, and the reported usage matched the API's `usage`.
- **Images**: a solid red and a solid blue 64×64 PNG with "Is this image
predominantly red?" on each model. Every request was sent as JSON with
`state.messages`, and each model separated the colors (red ≥ 0.989, blue
≤ 0.0023). Reported usage equals the API's raw `usage` in every case
(261 input tokens on mammoth/elephant/joey, 729 on bison/groundhog).
- `experimental_decide` with an image and Choice, Boolean, and Score
questions on bison-1 passes core validation with no warnings.
- **Image data through `experimental_decide`**: a `Buffer`, a base64
string, and a data URL string each produce the same
`data:image/png;base64,…` URL; an `image/*` part is detected as PNG; a
URL with `createDownload()` is downloaded and sent as
`data:image/jpeg;base64,…` (cat 0.9997), and without
`experimental_download` it throws before any request.
- **Formats**: inline JPEG (`comic-cat.png` converted to JPEG) answers
`animal`; an inline WebP landscape answers `landscape` on groundhog-1
and bison-1.
- **Order**: two images introduced as "Image 1:" and "Image 2:" (red
then blue, and blue then red) on groundhog-1, bison-1, and joey-1: the
answer for each image follows its position (≥ 0.988 for the red image, ≤
0.009 for the blue one).
- **Option budget**: 256 yes/no questions (512 options), 3 × 170 Choice
options, and 51 × 10 Score levels are accepted; 257 yes/no questions, 3
× 171 Choice options, and 52 × 10 Score levels are rejected with `422 …
512 per request`, matching the client-side check.
- **Remote URLs**: an HTTPS image URL on Google Cloud Storage works (cat
0.9996, dog 0.00008); `http://` and HTTPS URLs on other hosts are
rejected by the API with `422 Remote images require an allowed HTTPS
hostname on port 443`.
- `pnpm tsx src/decide/baseten/basic.ts` and `pnpm tsx
src/decide/baseten/image.ts` from `examples/ai-functions` both succeed
(image example: `cat` 0.99997, usage 780 input / 2 output tokens).
- Raw requests confirmed the API accepts null Score levels and `null`
yes/no criteria, rejects partial yes/no criteria and Box questions with
422, and accepts a 28,910-token state on bison-1.

Fixtures are unchanged live responses; see
`packages/baseten/src/__fixtures__/README.md`.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] A _patch_ changeset for relevant packages has been added (for bug
fixes / features - run `pnpm changeset` in the project root)
- [x] I have reviewed this pull request (self-review)

Checks run: `pnpm test` in `packages/baseten` (node and edge, 100/100),
`pnpm type-check` in `packages/baseten`, `pnpm exec ultracite check` on
the changed files, `pnpm verify:model-capabilities-docs`, and `pnpm
konsistent:check`.

- **Image data through `experimental_decide`**: a `Buffer`, a base64
string, and a data URL string each produce the same
`data:image/png;base64,…` URL; an `image/*` part is detected as PNG; a
URL with `createDownload()` is downloaded and sent as
`data:image/jpeg;base64,…` (cat 0.9997), and without
`experimental_download` it throws before any request.
- **Formats**: inline JPEG (`comic-cat.png` converted to JPEG) answers
`animal`; an inline WebP landscape answers `landscape` on groundhog-1
and bison-1.
- **Order**: two images introduced as "Image 1:" and "Image 2:" (red
then blue, and blue then red) on groundhog-1, bison-1, and joey-1: the
answer for each image follows its position (≥ 0.988 for the red image, ≤
0.009 for the blue one).
- **Option budget**: 256 yes/no questions (512 options), 3 × 170 Choice
options, and 51 × 10 Score levels are accepted; 257 yes/no questions, 3
× 171 Choice options, and 52 × 10 Score levels are rejected with `422 …
512 per request`, matching the client-side check.
- **Remote URLs**: an HTTPS image URL on Google Cloud Storage works (cat
0.9996, dog 0.00008); `http://` and HTTPS URLs on other hosts are
rejected by the API with `422 Remote images require an allowed HTTPS
hostname on port 443`.
- `pnpm tsx src/decide/baseten/basic.ts` and `pnpm tsx
src/decide/baseten/image.ts` from `examples/ai-functions` both succeed
(image example: `cat` 0.99997, usage 780 input / 2 output tokens).
- Raw requests confirmed the API accepts null Score levels and `null`
yes/no criteria, rejects partial yes/no criteria and Box questions with
422, and accepts a 28,910-token state on bison-1.

commit.message:
docs(examples): add WebMCP shopping cart assistant (#25186)

## Background

The WebMCP transport and `createMCPTools` need a concrete example
showing their runtime boundaries: browser tools must read live page
state while model inference and provider credentials stay on the
backend.

This is **PR 3 of 4**, stacked on #25185 and targeting `aayush/235`. The
stack begins with the transport in #25184.

## Summary

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Browser as Browser: WebMCP + MCP client
    participant Backend as Backend: AI SDK
    participant Model as Model provider
    Browser->>Backend: Message and tool definitions
    Backend->>Model: Message and tool schemas
    Model->>Backend: Call getCart
    Backend->>Browser: Forward tool call
    Browser->>Browser: MCP client calls WebMCP executeTool
    Browser->>Backend: Tool result
    Backend->>Model: Continue with result
    Model->>Backend: Cart summary
    Backend->>Browser: Display answer
```
